```{r, include = FALSE}
# A chunk's code sits under "Show code": open when it is what the page is
# about (`fold = "open"`), closed when it only supports it (`fold = "closed"`,
# the default unless the page sets another); `fold = FALSE` shows it plain,
# and so is code of three lines or fewer.
# Its results stay outside, always shown.
.fold_src <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("source")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(source = function(x, options) {
  f <- if (is.null(options$fold)) "closed" else options$fold
  # short code -- three lines or fewer, a chunk or the part of one before
  # its next output -- is shown as it is: folded, it would hide less than
  # the fold itself takes
  if (isFALSE(f) || length(unlist(strsplit(x, "\n", fixed = TRUE))) <= 3L) {
    return(.fold_src(x, options))
  }
  paste0("\n\n<details", if (identical(f, "open")) " open", ">",
         "<summary>Show code</summary>\n\n",
         .fold_src(x, options), "\n\n</details>\n\n")
})
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fold = "open")   # this page: the code is the subject
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment  = "#>"
)
gt_ok <- requireNamespace("gt", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = gt_ok)
# The pictures of this page's tables: committed in inst/rtf-examples/articles/
# (made by data-raw/gen_article_shots.R, which renders the page with
# RTFREPORTER_ARTICLE_OUT set, so .keep() writes the RTF) and copied next to
# the article to be served.
.here <- normalizePath(".")
.keep <- function(x, file) {
  out <- Sys.getenv("RTFREPORTER_ARTICLE_OUT")
  if (!nzchar(out)) return(invisible(NULL))
  doc <- if (inherits(x, "rtf_document")) x
         else if (inherits(x, "rtfplot")) rtfreporter::rtf_figures(rtfreporter::rtf_document(), x)
         else rtfreporter::rtf_tables(rtfreporter::rtf_document(), x)
  rtfreporter::generate_rtfreport(doc, file.path(out, file), overwrite = TRUE)
  invisible(NULL)
}
.shot <- function(file) {
  # the package's folder: the one above this page with a DESCRIPTION
  root <- .here
  while (!file.exists(file.path(root, "DESCRIPTION")) && dirname(root) != root) root <- dirname(root)
  src <- file.path(root, "inst", "rtf-examples", "articles", file)
  if (!file.exists(src)) return(invisible(NULL))
  dir.create(file.path(.here, "figures", "articles"), showWarnings = FALSE,
             recursive = TRUE)
  file.copy(src, file.path(.here, "figures", "articles", file), overwrite = TRUE)
  knitr::include_graphics(file.path("figures", "articles", file), error = FALSE)
}
```

```{r setup, eval = TRUE, fold = FALSE}
library(rtfreporter)
```

```{r, include = FALSE, eval = !gt_ok}
cat("This vignette renders only when the `gt` package is installed.\n")
```

> **The second path.** This article is about bringing a table you already
> have.  When the statistics are in a cards / cardx ARD, the recommended route
> is a table plan -- see [Get started](rtfreporter.html) and
> [Tables from an ARD](tables-from-ard.html).

The [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com) package by Posit gives users a
friendly grammar for *display tables* -- `cols_label()`,
`tab_header()`, `tab_spanner()`, `cols_align()`,
`tab_source_note()`, `tab_footnote()`, ...  Clinical summary tables are
very often produced by [gtsummary](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/)
(`tbl_summary()`, `tbl_regression()`, ...) or
[tfrmt](https://gsk-biostatistics.github.io/tfrmt/), both of which
ultimately render to a `gt_tbl`.  When you move from the HTML world to
the clinical TFL world, you want that same metadata to flow into the
RTF document -- not be re-stated in a different vocabulary.

## The recommended workflow: `as_rtftables()`

`as_rtftables()` is the single entry point.  It takes a table object
(`gt_tbl`, a **gtsummary** table, a `data.frame`/tibble, or a list of
these), reads all of the table's metadata, paginates the body, and
returns a list of ready-to-render `rtftable()` objects -- one per page:

```
  gt / gtsummary / tfrmt          as_rtftables()             rtf_tables()
  ------------------------  ->  read metadata + paginate  ->  add to doc  ->  generate_rtfreport()
        (a gt_tbl)               (list of rtftable pages)      (titles /
                                                                footnotes
                                                                flow through)
```

```{r}
library(gt)

g <- gt(head(mtcars, 3)) |>
  cols_label(mpg = "MPG", cyl = "Cyl", disp = "Disp", hp = "HP",
             drat = "Drat", wt = "WT", qsec = "QSec",
             vs = "VS", am = "AM", gear = "Gear", carb = "Carb") |>
  tab_header(
    title    = "Table 14.1.1",
    subtitle = "Demographics and baseline characteristics"
  ) |>
  tab_source_note("Source: built-in mtcars dataset.")

pages <- as_rtftables(g)          # read_meta = TRUE by default
length(pages)                      # one page here
class(pages[[1]])
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fold = FALSE}
.keep(pages, "gt_basic.rtf")
.shot("gt_basic.png")
```

Hand the pages straight to `rtf_tables()`.  The page-level title and
source notes travel with each page (as `rtf_titles` / `rtf_footnotes`
attributes) and are picked up automatically:

```{r}
doc <- rtf_document() |>
  rtf_section(page = 1, header = NULL, footer = NULL) |>
  rtf_tables(pages)

doc$contents[[1]]$title       # title + subtitle, read from the gt object
doc$contents[[1]]$footnote    # source note
```

For a single page you can use the convenience wrapper `as_rtftable()`,
which returns one `rtftable` instead of a list:

```{r}
tbl <- as_rtftable(g)   # == as_rtftables(g, split = "none")[[1]]
class(tbl)
```

## gtsummary in one line

A gtsummary table is converted to a `gt_tbl` automatically (via
`gtsummary::as_gt()`), so the workflow is identical:

```{r, eval = gt_ok && requireNamespace("gtsummary", quietly = TRUE)}
library(gtsummary)

s <- tbl_summary(
  trial[c("age", "grade", "response", "trt")],
  by = trt
)

pages <- as_rtftables(s)

doc <- rtf_document() |>
  rtf_section(page = 1, header = NULL, footer = NULL) |>
  rtf_tables(pages)

out <- tempfile(fileext = ".rtf")
generate_rtfreport(doc, out, overwrite = TRUE)
file.exists(out)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fold = FALSE, eval = gt_ok && requireNamespace("gtsummary", quietly = TRUE)}
.keep(doc, "gt_summary.rtf")
.shot("gt_summary.png")
```

Everything structural -- column labels, spanning headers, the stub / group
rows with their indentation, footnote texts and marks -- comes through.
Visual details such as bold group-header rows are dropped (see *Limitations*
below).

## Splitting a long table across pages

`as_rtftables()` splits a table that is too tall for one page; pass
`split` and `max_rows`:

```{r}
long <- data.frame(
  Parameter = sprintf("Row %02d", 1:8),
  Value     = round(rnorm(8), 2),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
pages <- as_rtftables(long, split = "group_force", max_rows = 4,
                      group_col = "Parameter")
length(pages)                       # 2 pages
vapply(pages, function(p) nrow(p$data), integer(1))
```

Per-cell styles read from a gt object are sliced to match each page
automatically.

## What gets read

`read_meta = TRUE` (the default) reads every token below.  Pass
`read_meta = c("col_header", "titles")` to read only some of them, or
`read_meta = FALSE` to read none.

* `"col_header"`     -- `cols_label()` -> the column header
* `"alignment"`      -- `cols_align()` -> each column's alignment
* `"spanning"`       -- `tab_spanner()` -> spanning header rows
* `"widths"`         -- `cols_width()` -> column widths (`"NNpx"` or `"NN%"`)
* `"titles"`         -- `tab_caption()` and `tab_header(title, subtitle)` ->
                        the page titles
* `"footnotes"`      -- `tab_footnote()` texts, then `tab_source_note()` ->
                        the page footnotes
* `"footnote_marks"` -- the footnote marks gt prints on column labels,
                        spanning headers, the title and row-group labels ->
                        `^{N}` superscripts, in gt's order, so the marks
                        match the notes (in-cell marks are always written
                        as `^{N}`)
* `"styles"`         -- explicit `tab_style()` declarations -> bold, italic,
                        underline, alignment and borders, plus body text
                        colour

Some things are always done, with no token: hidden columns are dropped,
the stub and row-group rows are placed in the body (group rows indented under
their heading), and stray HTML in cells is removed (`<br>` becomes a line
break).

A token you leave out falls back to the rtfreporter default (e.g. column
names from `names(data)`).  A token that no table source knows is an error.

## End-to-end example: a TFL-style adverse-events table

This is the kind of table you would normally build by hand:

```{r}
ae <- data.frame(
  SOC = c("Nervous system disorders",
          "Nervous system disorders",
          "Nervous system disorders",
          "Gastrointestinal disorders",
          "Gastrointestinal disorders"),
  PT  = c("Headache", "Dizziness", "Insomnia",
          "Nausea",   "Diarrhoea"),
  Placebo_n = c("10 (33.3)", "2 ( 6.7)", "3 (10.0)",
                "6 (20.0)",  "4 (13.3)"),
  Active_n  = c("13 (43.3)", "2 ( 6.7)", "4 (13.3)",
                "7 (23.3)",  "5 (16.7)"),
  Total_n   = c("23 (38.3)", "4 ( 6.7)", "7 (11.7)",
                "13 (21.7)", "9 (15.0)"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

ae_gt <-
  gt(ae, groupname_col = "SOC", rowname_col = "PT") |>
  cols_label(PT = "Preferred Term",
             Placebo_n = "Placebo",
             Active_n  = "Active",
             Total_n   = "Total") |>
  tab_stubhead(label = "SOC / PT") |>
  cols_align("right", columns = c(Placebo_n, Active_n, Total_n)) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Treatment Arm",
              columns = c(Placebo_n, Active_n, Total_n)) |>
  tab_header(title    = "Table 14.2.1",
             subtitle = "Adverse Events Summary (Safety Population)") |>
  tab_source_note("Source: ADaM ADAE.") |>
  tab_footnote("Percentages are based on column N.")
```

Convert it with `as_rtftables()` and add the pages to a document:

```{r}
doc <- rtf_document() |>
  rtf_section(
    page   = 1,
    header = rtf_header(rows = list(c(l = "Protocol RTF-101",
                                       r = "Page {AUTO_PAGE}"))),
    footer = NULL
  ) |>
  rtf_tables(as_rtftables(ae_gt))
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fold = FALSE}
.keep(doc, "gt_ae.rtf")
.shot("gt_ae.png")
```


`doc$contents[[1L]]$content` now has:

```{r}
tbl <- doc$contents[[1L]]$content
nrow(tbl$data)          # 5 PT rows + 2 SOC group rows
tbl$data$rowname[1:3]   # the SOC's heading row, then its first two PTs, indented
tbl$col_header          # spanner row + stubhead-labelled bottom row
```

Page-level blocks:

```{r}
doc$contents[[1L]]$title      # title + subtitle
doc$contents[[1L]]$footnote   # footnote text + source note (in that order)
```

Render to RTF:

```{r}
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".rtf")
generate_rtfreport(doc, out, overwrite = TRUE)
file.exists(out)
```

## Precedence: explicit arguments beat gt-extracted values

The translation honours the documented precedence chain.  If you
specify `col_header = c("A", "B", ...)` explicitly, gt's
`cols_label()` is ignored for that table:

```{r}
g <- gt(head(mtcars, 1)[, "mpg", drop = FALSE]) |>
  cols_label(mpg = "MPG")
tbl <- as_rtftable(g, read_meta = TRUE, col_header = "Override")
tbl$col_header[[1L]]
```

The same applies to:

| Slot                  | Explicit arg                 |
|-----------------------|------------------------------|
| Column header         | `col_header`                 |
| Per-column alignment  | `col_spec[[j]]$align`        |
| Spanner stack         | (passed via `col_header`)    |
| Absolute widths       | `column_widths_twips`        |
| Relative widths       | `col_rel_width`              |
| Page titles           | `rtf_titles()`               |
| Page footnotes        | `rtf_footnotes()`            |

Per-column `col_spec` entries are **deep-merged** -- a user-supplied
`align = "left"` for column 1 only knocks out gt's column-1
alignment, the other columns keep gt's values.

## Limitations

The following gt / gtsummary features depend on HTML/CSS rendering that
RTF cannot reproduce, so they are intentionally **not** carried through:

* **Bold group-header rows.**  Applied by gtsummary through
  `tab_style()` in a way that the style reader does not currently map
  to a whole-row attribute.  (Cell-level `tab_style(cell_text(...))`
  *is* read -- see the `"styles"` token.)
* **Cell background colour / fill.**  Not read.
* **Markdown inside titles / labels.**  `md("**bold**")` is flattened
  to plain text: the `**` markers are removed.
* **`column_width` strings other than `"NNpx"` or `"NN%"`.**  Mixed-unit
  widths bail out to `NULL` and the renderer falls back to its default
  proportional split.
